usage: wsp commit <thread> [--message "<message>"] [--file <path>]...
  commits every changed file in the folder the thread works in, other threads'
  changes there included, or the files named; without a message the thread's
  agent drafts one

  --message    the commit message, a subject line, a blank line, then the body,
               -m for short; the thread's agent drafts it without one
  --file       a file to commit, by path from the checkout's top, once per file;
               every changed file without one
  --json       print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
               everything else on stderr
  --state      the state file the host serves
  --host       run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
               hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp discard <thread> <path> [--yes]
  puts one changed file in the folder the thread works in back as its last
  commit has it, or removes it where that has none

  --yes      go ahead without being asked
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp fix <thread> [--check "<name>" | --child <thread>]
  asks the thread's agent to fix a failed check or merge a child, or updates its
  folder from its base and asks it to fix what conflicts

  --check    the failed check to send, by its name on the pull request; without
             it the folder is updated from its base and a conflict is sent
  --child    a child thread whose merge into this thread's folder stopped on
             conflicts, by its id or a prefix; this thread's agent is asked to
             merge it and resolve them, and nothing is updated
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp merge in <lead> <child>
  merges a child thread's branch into its lead's folder with a merge commit, or
  names the files that conflict

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp merge <thread> [--method merge|squash|rebase] [--when-checks-pass]
  merges the pull request of the thread's branch, or merges it once its checks
  pass

  --method              merge, squash or rebase; the repository's own default
                        without one
  --when-checks-pass    merge once the checks pass rather than now, where the
                        repository allows it
  --json                print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line,
                        with everything else on stderr
  --state               the state file the host serves
  --host                run the line against a host on your account, by the name
                        wsp hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole
                        shell

usage: wsp rename <workspace> "<name>"
  names the workspace on this computer; the name is unique here, so one another
  workspace holds is refused

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp fork <workspace> [--name <n>] [--size <cpu>x<memGb>]
       [--send "<task>" [run's flags]]
  a new machine from the source's image version, on the source's branch with its
  commits pushed first, not a copy of its live disk; --size as new's, the
  person's alone

  --name            what to call the new machine; <source>-fork without it
  --size            the machine size as <cpu>x<memGb>, like 2x4; a size the
                    provider does not offer is refused naming the ones it does
  --send            a message for the new machine's first thread, with run's own
                    flags after it
  --agent           which agent runs the thread, by its catalog id (claude,
                    codex, opencode, cursor); the project's own default without
                    it
  --model           the model the turn runs on, by the agent's own slug
                    (claude-sonnet-5); the thread's own without it
  --effort          how hard the agent thinks, by its own word (low, medium,
                    high, xhigh, max); absent on a new thread means the agent's
                    default; on send, the thread's own
  --access          how far the agent may go without asking: ask, auto-edit,
                    full or plan, refused where the agent has no such mode;
                    without it, the project's, else the agent's default, else
                    full
  --cwd             the folder on the machine to work in; the project's folder
                    without it
  --notify          where each turn's end is sent, a thread's id or me; repeats
  --max-machines    how many machines may stand at once under one root thread;
                    defaults to 3
  --max-depth       how many levels of threads may stand under the root thread;
                    defaults to 2
  --json            print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line,
                    with everything else on stderr
  --state           the state file the host serves
  --host            run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                    hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell
